Benign.meaning: Non-cancerous, non-invasive cellular growth. Cell nuclei maintain organized architecture without cytological features of malignancy.

Malignant.meaning: Carcinomatous, cytologically malignant cells displaying marked pleomorphism, high nuclear area, irregular contours, and chromatin condensation.
Malignant.stage_relevance: Diagnostic confirmation only. Tumor stage (TNM: T1-T4, N0-N3, M0-M1) must be determined through histopathology, surgical margins, and distant staging scans.

clinical_warning: Diagnostic labels (Benign / Malignant) indicate cytopathological classification of malignancy. They must NOT be confused with cancer stages (Stage 0 - Stage IV).
imaging_modality: Fine Needle Aspirate (FNA) digitized cytological nuclear microscopy

attributes.description: Unique anonymized identification number corresponding to the patient aspirate sample.
Pathologist-confirmed clinical diagnostic label for the fine needle aspirate.

attributes.computation: Mean of distances from the center of the cell nucleus to perimeter points.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Malignant nuclei are typically significantly larger (nuclear enlargement / macro-karyosis).

attributes.computation: Standard deviation of gray-scale pixel values within the nuclear boundary.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Quantifies chromatin clumpiness and nuclear hyperchromasia typical of cancer.

attributes.computation: Mean perimeter length bounding the segmented cell nuclei.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Measures nuclear size and circumferential irregularity.

attributes.computation: Area enclosed within the nuclear contour, measured by pixel count scaled to microns.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Enlarged nuclear area strongly correlates with mitotic index and aggressive tumors.

attributes.computation: Local variation in radial lengths measured along the nuclear perimeter.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Smooth contours characterize normal nuclei; jagged irregular boundaries reflect malignancy.

attributes.computation: (perimeter^2 / area - 1.0).
attributes.clinical_relevance: High compactness indicates complex convoluted nuclear borders.

attributes.computation: Severity of concave portions (indentations) of the nuclear contour.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Severe nuclear groove indents and clefts are prominent cytological hallmarks of carcinoma.

attributes.computation: Number of distinct concave portions along the nuclear contour.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Higher count of concave notches directly reflects malignant membrane folding.

attributes.computation: Relative length differences between perpendicular chords bisecting the nucleus.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Malignant transformation disrupts nuclear polarity and produces asymmetrical nuclei.

attributes.computation: Mandelbrot coastline approximation [fractal dimension - 1.0].
attributes.clinical_relevance: High fractal dimension indicates complex microscopic boundary irregularities.

attributes.computation: Standard error of nuclear radius across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Anisokaryosis (variation in nuclear size between adjacent cells).

attributes.computation: Standard error of nuclear texture across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Heterogeneity of nuclear staining and chromatin condensation.

attributes.computation: Standard error of perimeter length across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Circumferential size variation across the aspirate.

attributes.computation: Standard error of nuclear area across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Area variation reflects uncontrolled growth rate variability.

attributes.computation: Standard error of perimeter smoothness across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Contour variation between cells.

attributes.computation: Standard error of compactness across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Shape variability across the aspirate.

attributes.computation: Standard error of concavity across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Variation in depth of nuclear indentations.

attributes.computation: Standard error of concave point count across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Variation in notch frequency.

attributes.computation: Standard error of symmetry across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Asymmetry variance between cells.

attributes.computation: Standard error of fractal dimension across cell population in sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Boundary complexity variance.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three largest nuclear radii recorded in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Isolates the most aggressive / giant tumor cells.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three most variable texture readings in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Isolates maximum nuclear hyperchromasia and chromatin irregularity.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three largest perimeters recorded in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Maximum nuclear perimeter in sample.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three largest nuclear areas recorded in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: One of the single most discriminative features for invasive malignancy.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three worst smoothness values in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Maximum membrane jaggedness.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three highest compactness values in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Extreme boundary distortion.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three highest concavity values in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Severe nuclear clefts in malignant clones.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three highest concave point counts in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: High discriminative power for cytological malignancy.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three most asymmetrical nucleus readings in the sample.
attributes.clinical_relevance: Maximum architectural distortion.

attributes.computation: Mean of the three highest fractal dimension readings in the sample.
